children: backed OpenAI is reportedly exploring a new funding round that could value the ChatGPT maker at roughly $1.2 trillion, a sharp step up from its $852 billion valuation in March and another sign that private investors remain willing to pay aggressively for AI growth. The potential deal would give OpenAI more capital to fund infrastructure and model development while also allowing it to delay an IPO that CEO Sam Altman has already ruled out for 2026.
The proposed valuation would represent an increase of about 41% from OpenAI's latest private-market mark.
According to the Financial Times, discussions with large investors are still at an early stage, meaning both the size of the round and the final valuation could change.
The higher valuation is being supported by rapid revenue growth.

OpenAI generated $6.7 billion in revenue during the second quarter, up from $5.7 billion in the first quarter. The company has also said it now serves more than 1 billion active users and over 200 million businesses.
Demand for Codex, its AI coding product, has added another growth engine, while OpenAI recently introduced Astra, its latest advanced AI model.
The challenge is that expenses are rising almost as quickly. Operating margins have been declining as OpenAI spends heavily on computing infrastructure, model training and product development.
That makes continued access to private capital especially important.
The fundraising discussions also follow Altman's decision not to pursue an IPO this year, with AI-safety concerns cited as one factor.
A $1.2 trillion valuation would raise expectations considerably.

Investors should watch whether OpenAI can keep quarterly revenue growth near current levels while improving operating margins and controlling infrastructure costs. A continued surge in enterprise adoption, Codex usage and monetization would help justify the premium.

The risk is that private valuations keep rising faster than profits. If growth slows or AI infrastructure spending continues to pressure margins, a future IPO could face a much tougher valuation test.

The timing also matters because Anthropic is reportedly moving toward a possible IPO, increasing pressure on OpenAI to prove that staying private is creating more value rather than simply postponing public-market scrutiny.

title: OpenAI Eyes Stunning $1.2 Trillion Valuation
